extra.message: Session Cookie Forgery (No Integrity Protection) — Complete account takeover; an attacker can impersonate any user by crafting a valid session cookie. [verified: Session cookie is a base64-encoded JSON object without HMAC or server-side storage; any attacker can forge a cookie with any username, enabling impersonation.]

SQL Injection in User Login — An attacker can bypass authentication, exfiltrate credentials, or gain unauthorized access to the system. [verified: The login function at libuser.py:12 directly uses string formatting to inject user-supplied username and password into a SQL query without any escaping or sanitization. No compensating input validation or prepared statements are present, and the endpoint is publicly reachable.]

Missing Authorization on Post Listing — Unauthorized disclosure of all user posts, allowing an attacker to read private messages and enumerate users. [verified: The route /api/post/<username> at line 47-51 has no authentication or authorization check; any user can call it and retrieve all posts for any username via libposts.get_posts.]

Potential SQL Injection in Post View — Data extraction, corruption, or unauthorized access to database [verified: Username from URL path is passed directly to libposts.get_posts without any sanitization or validation. No evidence of parameterized queries or other controls in the provided code.]

Weak Flask Secret Key — Full account takeover via forged session cookies [verified: Flask's SECRET_KEY is hardcoded as 'aaaaaaa', a weak and easily guessable value. This allows an attacker to forge any user's session cookie, leading to account takeover without additional authentication checks.]

Hardcoded Fernet Session Key — Session hijacking – attacker can decrypt existing cookies or forge new ones to impersonate any user, gaining full web session access. [verified: The Fernet encryption key is hardcoded in libsession.py line 9. An attacker with access to the source code can decrypt any session cookie to extract the username and country, and forge valid cookies to impersonate users, bypassing the country-based session integrity check.]

Missing Authorization on Post Listing Endpoint — An attacker can read all posts of any user, revealing private messages or sensitive information. [verified: The /api/post/<username> endpoint at line 49-53 calls libposts.get_posts(username) without any authentication or authorization check, allowing any unauthenticated attacker to retrieve all posts for any username.]

Cross-Site Request Forgery on post creation and password change — An attacker can force an authenticated user to create posts or change their password, leading to data corruption, account takeover, or abuse of the posting functionality. [verified: Endpoint mod_posts.do_create (line 35) uses session-based auth without CSRF token or SameSite cookie; any authenticated user can be tricked into forging a POST. The password change endpoint (mod_user.do_chpasswd_post, line 85) has the same absence of CSRF protection.]

Missing authorization allows viewing any user's posts — An unauthenticated attacker can view the posts of any user, leading to information disclosure of all user posts. [verified: The do_view function in mod_posts.py (line 12-18) accepts a username from the URL and calls libposts.get_posts(username) without any authentication or authorization check, allowing an unauthenticated attacker to view any user's posts.]
